persona.title: Pretend you are…
persona.text: Pretend you are Dorothy, 81, in Illinois. Your email is full of ads, a few scary messages and the notes from your family you actually want. Your son Tom's emails get buried. Today your granddaughter helps you set up Porchlight, a calm helper for your mail and your to-do list. (You will only see EXAMPLE emails — never connect a real email account in this test.)

challenge.intro: Now you are Dorothy. Porchlight starts brand new. Nobody will tell you which button to press. Use what you learned. When it asks which email you use, choose Yahoo Mail — never Gmail. When you finish, tap Check my work.
challenge.start: Open Porchlight with the normal link. If you see 'Welcome to Porchlight' with the big blue 'Let's get started' button, it is already empty — begin. Otherwise tap ⚙️ My Setup at the bottom right, scroll down to the card 'Start fresh', tap 'Erase my information' → 'Yes, erase everything'. You should now see 'Welcome to Porchlight'.

tasks.text: Set Porchlight up for yourself: your name is Dorothy, and you want your helper to be called Grace. Finish the set-up questions until you reach your Home page.
tasks.hint: Tap 'Let's get started'. The first question is your name, the second is the helper's name — tap Grace. Keep tapping Next (choose Yahoo Mail, not Gmail) until 'Take me to my Home page'.

tasks.text: Your son Tom's emails must always come first. Tell Porchlight.
tasks.hint: One set-up question asks 'Whose emails should always come first?'. Type Tom and tap 'Add this person'. Missed it? The ⚙️ settings let you go through the questions again.

tasks.text: Your eyes are tired. Make the words in Porchlight the BIGGEST size.
tasks.hint: The last set-up question is 'How big should the words be?'. Choose Biggest (not Big or Bigger).

tasks.text: Your daughter Sarah's example email asks about Sunday dinner. Put a reminder about it on your to-do list.
tasks.hint: Tap 'Go through my mail', then 'Help me answer' under Sarah's email. Inside it there is a button 'Add to my to-do list'.

tasks.text: Add this to your to-do list yourself: Call the pharmacy about my refill.
tasks.hint: Tap the ☑️ To-Do button at the bottom (in the middle). Type it in 'Add something to remember' and tap 'Add to my list'.

ownWords.question: In your own words, what is this app for?
keyIdeas: a calm helper for email and a to-do list, made for older adults
it sorts email and warns you about scams
it can turn an email into a to-do and keep your list

lines: Welcome. This short video explains Porchlight: what it is for, and how to use it.
First, the problem. Real notes from family get buried under adverts, and some emails are scams made to look urgent.
Porchlight is a patient helper. It sorts your email, reads it out loud, and helps you write back.
It is for anyone who dreads their inbox, especially older adults who want big words and plain language.
Porchlight reads your real Gmail when you open it inside Claude, with your own Claude account. The try-it page uses example emails.
It starts with easy questions, one at a time. Tap Let's get started. Read this to me reads any question aloud.
Type the name you'd like to be called, and tap Next. Then name your helper: Sunny, Grace, Buddy, Penny, or your own.
What would you like help with? Sort my email, My calendar, My to-do list, Weather, a joke or Bible verse, and more. Tap all you want.
Which email do you use? Gmail connects directly. For others, it shows how to send a copy to a free Gmail account.
Tap Connect my Gmail, then Allow. If Google asks you to sign in, your password goes into Google, never into Porchlight.
Whose emails should come first? Your children, your doctor, your church. Type a name, and tap Add this person.
Last, pick a word size: Big, Bigger or Biggest. Then tap Take me to my Home page.
Your Home page greets you by name and shows only what you asked for, in big cards.
Along the bottom are five buttons: Home, Mail, To-Do, Talk, and My Setup. Help sits at the top of every screen.
Tap Go through my mail, and it sorts your newest emails into four groups.
Needs your answer comes first. Then Be careful, may be a scam. Then Good to know. Last, Can wait, for adverts and newsletters.
Each email says why it is there. Tap Read it to open one. Read it to me says it out loud. Explain it simply tells you what it wants.
For a scam, tap Show me why. Here, Amazon is spelled with a zero. Porchlight says it plainly: be careful, and don't click.
To answer, tap Help me answer. Say what you mean in the top box, tap Write it for me, and change anything you like.
Then tap Send my answer. It asks once more, and nothing goes until you tap Yes, send it. Or tap Save it as a draft instead.
Finished with one? Tap I'm done with this, and it moves out of the way.
On the To-Do page, type something to remember, tap Add to my list, and tap the big box when it's done.
On the Talk page, chat with your helper. Paste a text message you got, and it tells you if it looks like a scam.
Next to it, Family notes is a board your invited family can write on too.
My Setup lets you redo the questions, change the word size, or erase everything and start fresh.
To start, sit down once with someone you trust and answer the questions. Then each morning, open your Home page, go through your mail, and begin at the top.
Porchlight never asks for your passwords, and sends nothing unless you tap Send and say yes. Your answers stay on this device, or in your own Claude account.
Porchlight is twenty-nine dollars, once. The profits help students in Kenya stay in school.
Stuck? Tap Help at the top of any screen. It explains the page you are on, in plain words.

daily.task: Add or change one thing in Porchlight — for example check a made-up message, or add a made-up trusted person.

explore.name: 👋 Setup questions
explore.find: It opens here the first time. Tap “Let's get started”.
explore.try: Answer each question: your name, the helper’s name, what you want help with, email, important people, zip code, websites, verse or joke, word size. Try Back and “Skip for now”.

explore.name: 🏠 Home
explore.find: Tap “Take me to my Home page”, or “Home” in the bar at the bottom.
explore.try: Tap every card: “Go through my mail”, “Open my list”, Weather “Open ↗”, “Today's price ↗”, “Open family notes”. Try “Read the verse to me” or “Tell me another”.

explore.name: 📬 Mail
explore.find: Tap “Mail” in the bar at the bottom.
explore.try: Tap “Go through my mail”. On an email tap “Show me why”, “Read it”, “I'm done with this”. Tap “Check for new mail” and “Show emails I finished”.

explore.name: ✉️ One email
explore.find: On Mail, tap “Read it” on any email.
explore.try: Tap “Explain it simply” and “Add to my to-do list”. Tap “Help me answer”, type a reply, tap “Write it for me”. Look at “Send my answer”, don’t send. Tap Close.

explore.name: ✅ To-Do
explore.find: Tap “To-Do” in the bar at the bottom.
explore.try: Type a to-do and tap “Add to my list”. Tick it done, then not done. Remove one. Tap “Clear finished items”.

explore.name: 💬 Talk
explore.find: Tap “Talk” in the bar at the bottom.
explore.try: Tap each idea button, like “Tell me a joke”. Type a message and tap Send. Tap Stop while it answers. Tap “Start a new talk”.

explore.name: 📝 Family notes
explore.find: Tap “Talk” at the bottom, then “Family notes” at the top.
explore.try: Write a short test note and tap “Post my note”. Tap “Read it to me”. Remove your test note.

explore.name: ⚙️ My Setup
explore.find: Tap “My Setup” in the bar at the bottom.
explore.try: Change Word size to Big, Bigger, Biggest. Read Connections. Tap “Answer the setup questions again”. Leave “Start fresh” for the very end.

explore.name: ❔ Help
explore.find: Tap the “Help” button at the top of the page.
explore.try: Open Help on each screen: the words change. Read “Staying safe”. Tap “Ask … a question” (it shows your helper’s name). Tap Close.

explore.name: ❓ The round ? button
explore.find: Tap the round ? in the bottom corner.
explore.try: Open each line: text size (Aa), Ask an AI, More from Daraja, Which AI do you use, See it as a new user, Help. Close it. Leave “Start fresh” for the very end.
